message.content:
**Three major schisms in Christian history**

| # | Name & Year | What it was |
|---|-------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** – 1054 | The formal split between the Eastern (Byzantine/Orthodox) churches and the Western (Roman Catholic) church, largely over issues of papal primacy, theology, liturgy, and cultural differences. |
| 2 | **Western Schism (Papal Schism)** – 1378 – 1417 | A period during which rival claimants to the papacy existed simultaneously (the Avignon Papacy, the Roman line, and later the Pisan line), leading to divisions within the Latin Church itself. |
| 3 | **Protestant Reformation** – 1517 – 1648 (and beyond) | Initiated by Martin Luther’s 95 Theses in 1517, this movement led to the creation of numerous Protestant denominations and fundamentally altered the religious landscape of Europe, challenging doctrines, practices, and ecclesiastical authority of the Roman Catholic Church. |

These three events are commonly referred to as the “great” or “major” schisms in Christian history because each caused lasting theological, political, and cultural divisions that shaped the development of Christianity worldwide.
